chunks: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) asking him
about the animals from which al-Khazz is made from their fur — are they predators?
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Al-Husayn ibn Ali and after him my grandfather (peace be upon them both) wore al-Khazz.

key_terms.الدَّوَابّ: Animals (beasts of burden or animals in general)
key_terms.الْخَزّ: Al-Khazz: a fabric made from silk woven with animal fur/wool, subject of jurisprudential debate on permissibility
key_terms.جَدِّي: My grandfather (referring to an ancestor of Imam al-Ridha among the Imams)
key_terms.سِبَاع: Predatory animals/beasts of prey — wearing garments from such animals is generally prohibited
key_terms.وَبَر: Fur/wool of an animal (not feathers or hair)

ai.seo_question: Is wearing al-Khazz permissible in Islam? What did Imam al-Ridha say about al-Khazz fabric?
ai.summary: This hadith records Ja'far ibn 'Isa's written inquiry to Imam al-Ridha (AS) asking whether the animals whose fur is used to make al-Khazz (a fine fabric woven from silk mixed with animal wool or fur) are predators — which would affect its permissibility. The Imam's written reply establishes the permissibility of wearing al-Khazz by invoking the precedent of Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali and the Imam's own grandfather (likely Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Baqir), indicating their practice constitutes authoritative evidence. The context reflects the Shia jurisprudential method of appealing to Imamic precedent to resolve questions of ritual permissibility.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ja’far Bin Isa who said, 
‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup>
about the animals from which Al-Khazz is made, from their fur, is it a predator?’
So heasws wrote: ‘Al-Husaynasws Bin Aliasws wore Al-Khazz, and from after himasws, myasws grandfatherasws’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ja‘far ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about animals from the fur of which al- Khazz is made; if such animals are of predators.’
He (the Imam) wrote in answer, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, wore al-Khazz (garments made from skin or fur of an animal that lives in water) then my grandfather also did so.’”
